metadata.title: Consequences of the Three-Dimensional Jacobian Counterexample for Seven Neighbouring Conjectures: Located Implications and Exactly Checked Witnesses
metadata.description:
Alpöge's explicit Keller map on C^3, with a three-point fibre, refutes the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension N >= 3. Seven neighbouring conjectures are tied to it by published implications whose dimension indices decide what the map refutes. We locate each implication in a primary text, record its theorem and index, and close the implications under composition into a status table with an evidence mark per entry. Exact computations over Q and Q(i) check the map and its fibre, a homogeneous-type test, a dimension-15 homogeneous witness, a dimension-48 gradient witness whose Hessian-nilpotent quartic has 382 monomials, and Long's rank-two Poisson map.

The Dixmier and Poisson conjectures fail at every index n >= 3, and the Poisson conjecture also at n = 2. The Mathieu conjecture fails for SU(N) with N >= 15 and, by Long, for SU(2). The Gaussian moments conjecture fails for n >= 3, and the vanishing, Hessian and symmetric forms fail with explicit witnesses. Every check is exact, so no interval applies, and each negative control fires. Mathieu's original paper was not located, so that row rests on an expository rendering. Dixmier at ranks 1 and 2, Poisson at index 1, Mathieu for 3 <= N <= 14 and the two-variable Jacobian conjecture stay open.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: Revision. New title stating what the results sustain. A status table of the Jacobian conjecture and seven neighbouring conjectures (Mathieu, Dixmier, Poisson, Gaussian moments, vanishing, Image, Hessian and symmetric forms), one row each, with the implication and its dimension index, the source theorem located, an evidence mark per ingredient ([MV], [D], [C], [V], [U]), the explicit witness with its dimension and the open indices, generated by a script from the experiment artifacts; an implication graph and an index map built from the same data. The Poisson row carries an exact in-house check of Long's rank-two map (computation EXP-144: bracket identities, determinant 1, three-point fibre, reducible R, two failing controls), so Poisson(n) is false for n >= 2 with index 1 open. A Methods section with five procedures in pseudocode (fibre by lex Groebner basis, homogeneous-type test, symmetrization with collision transport, de Bondt homogenization, Poisson-endomorphism check), each with inputs, arithmetic domain, software and measured cost, and propositions proving the soundness of every reduction; a Validation section with every independent route and its numbers; an Ablation section with the negative controls; a Related work section of 43 cited works, each characterised; the hash of every primary text read. Mathieu 1997 stays marked as not located and its Zwart rendering as read; Wilson and Zheglov are marked not verified.
